html:
The Shawnee are a Native American people of the Northeastern Woodlands who speak an Algonquian language. Their homeland before contact was probably in southern Ohio.

No people moved more. In the 1600s, pressed by the Haudenosaunee during the Beaver Wars, Shawnee groups scattered as far as Illinois, Pennsylvania and the Carolinas. In the 1700s they lived near the Lenape in Pennsylvania, then drifted back to the Ohio country, and a small group joined the Muscogee in Alabama.

They fought for over sixty years to keep their land:

  • the French and Indian War and Pontiac's War against the British
  • Lord Dunmore's War and the American Revolution against the colonists
  • the Northwest Indian War of 1786 to 1795
  • Tecumseh's confederacy and the War of 1812

After Tecumseh died in 1813 they signed away their land. Under the Indian Removal Act they were moved west of the Mississippi, and finally to Oklahoma, home of the three Shawnee tribes today.
